comments.headline: Trees Not Identified by Species or Mature Height
comments.summary: Landscape plan shows tree symbols without species identification or mature height notation. Trees cannot be verified as utility-compatible or differentiated as large trees (≥40 feet) per ECM Appendix F standards required for clearance compliance.
comments.crossDep: Austin Energy will need to verify species utility-compatibility per ECM Appendix F before approval
comments.attn: Verify species and mature heights against ECM Appendix F requirements before cross-referencing on landscape plan. Detail EL-2.10 flagged by single run; recommend confirmation across plant schedule and species list.

details.text: Proposed trees (Cedar Elm, Live Oak, Texas Mountain Laurel, Mexican Redbud) listed in plant schedule do not reference utility-compatible (UC) designation against ECM Appendix F. Non-UC trees must remain ≥15 feet from distribution conductors per UCM § 1.10.10.4.

runComments.comment: Plant schedule specifies Cedar Elm, Live Oak, Texas Mountain Laurel, and Mexican Redbud as proposed trees near overhead distribution line, but does not verify utility-compatible (UC) designation against ECM Appendix F. UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires non-utility-compatible trees to remain beyond 15 lateral feet of distribution conductors; applicant must document species verification against ECM Appendix F.

Non-utility-compatible trees may be proposed within 15 lateral feet of the overhead electric distribution conductor along the southern boundary. However, species cannot be verified from the landscape plan symbols, which show only generic tree circles labeled with category codes (M, PL, SYM) with no reference to the plant schedule species. Distance from conductor centerline to tree trunk cannot be verified due to lack of conductor position markings and clearance dimensions on the plan. Applicant must provide: (1) species identification for each tree symbol on landscape plan cross-referenced to plant schedule; (2) verification of UC status from ECM Appendix F for each species; (3) measured clearance dimensions from outside conductor (not pole center) to tree trunk center.

Three mitigation trees positioned near OHE line in southeast corner of landscape plan are shown at approximately 2-5 feet from conductor. Species identification not provided on landscape plan; cannot verify whether proposed trees are utility-compatible per ECM Appendix F without documented species verification.

details.text: Landscape plan tree symbols show only generic circles with category labels (M=mitigation, PL=parking lot, SYM) without species identification. Plant schedule lists species names but symbols are not cross-referenced to plant schedule, preventing identification of tree species.

runComments.comment: The landscape plan (Sheet 31) does not identify the species of trees proposed near electric facilities. The plant schedule on Sheet 35 clearly lists tree species (Cedar Elm, Live Oak, Texas Mountain Laurel, Mexican Redbud) with botanical names and specifications. However, the landscape plan symbols show only generic circles with category labels (M=mitigation, PL=parking lot, SYM) with no reference to the plant schedule or species identification. The tree symbols cannot be traced to specific species. This violates the requirement that trees shown on plans be identified. Applicant must provide: (1) landscape plan tree symbols keyed to plant schedule with species callouts; (2) for trees near electric facilities, species label on each symbol or clear legend cross-referencing symbols to species names.

details.text: Plant schedule (Sheet 35) specifies only planting heights (16 feet for shade trees, 8–10 feet for ornamentals), not mature heights. Large trees with mature height ≥40 feet per ECM Appendix F must remain ≥25 lateral feet from distribution conductors per UCM § 1.10.10.4.

runComments.comment: Plant schedule does not specify mature heights for proposed trees. UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires large trees (mature height ≥40 feet per ECM Appendix F) to remain ≥25 lateral feet from distribution conductors. Without mature height specifications, the applicant cannot verify this requirement is met.

Large trees (mature height 40+ feet per ECM Appendix F) may be proposed within 25 lateral feet of the overhead electric distribution conductor. The plant schedule (Sheet 35) lists species with sizes (Cedar Elm, Live Oak), but the landscape plan (Sheet 31) does not differentiate trees by size or mature height. Tree symbols on the landscape plan are shown only as generic circles with category labels (M, PL, SYM), with no notation of which trees are 'large' per ECM Appendix F standards. Measured clearance distances from conductor to tree trunks are also not provided. Applicant must provide: (1) identification of each tree symbol on landscape plan keyed to plant schedule; (2) mature height notation for each tree per ECM Appendix F; (3) measured clearance distances from outside conductor to tree trunk center for trees within 25 feet.

Three trees in southeast corner are positioned at 2-5 feet from OHE line, well within the 25-foot minimum clearance for large trees from distribution conductors. However, species identification of these three specific trees is not provided on landscape plan. Plant schedule lists Cedar Elm and Live Oak (both potentially large trees), but cannot verify which species are the three trees in southeast corner without explicit labeling. Mature heights in plant schedule (16' minimum) appear lower than typical ECM Appendix F values for these species (40+ feet), creating ambiguity about whether these are truly large trees per ECM Appendix F definition (mature height ≥ 40 feet).

details.text: Landscape plan does not differentiate large trees (mature height ≥40 feet) from other trees through size notation or visual differentiation. All tree symbols appear as identical generic circles, preventing identification of which trees are subject to stricter large-tree clearance requirements (25 feet distribution, 50 feet transmission).

runComments.comment: The grouping definition of 'large trees' is trees with mature height ≥40 feet per ECM Appendix F. The plant schedule (Sheet 35) does not specify mature heights for any proposed trees, listing only planting heights (16 feet for shade trees, 8-10 feet for ornamental trees). Without mature height information, large trees cannot be differentiated on the plans.

Large trees (mature height 40+ feet per ECM Appendix F) are not differentiated on the landscape plan to allow verification of clearances from overhead electric facilities. The plant schedule on Sheet 35 lists mature heights (e.g., Cedar Elm, Live Oak specifications with container sizes indicating mature trees), but the landscape plan (Sheet 31) does not show these heights or indicate which tree symbols represent large trees. All tree symbols appear as identical generic circles with only category labels (M, PL), providing no visual differentiation of size. Without height notation on the landscape plan, reviewers and inspectors cannot identify which trees are subject to the stricter 25-foot (distribution) or 50-foot (transmission) large-tree clearance requirements. Applicant must provide: (1) notation of mature height on each tree symbol on landscape plan, or (2) distinct symbol types or colors to differentiate large trees (40+ feet) from other trees, or (3) clear legend showing which species in the plant schedule meet the large-tree threshold and marking those trees accordingly on the landscape plan.

Plant schedule lists Cedar Elm and Live Oak with 16' HT minimum specifications, substantially lower than typical ECM Appendix F mature heights for these species. Landscape plan does not differentiate large trees from other trees or cross-reference to mature height designations. Without clear identification of which trees meet the 40+ feet mature height threshold per ECM Appendix F, large tree differentiation cannot be verified.

comments.headline: Clearance Distances & Measurement Reference Points Not Documented
comments.summary: Landscape plan contains no dimensioned clearance callouts showing distances from trees to electric facilities. Measurement reference points—outside conductor vs. pole centerline and tree trunk vs. canopy edge—are not specified, preventing verification of compliance.
comments.crossDep: Electrical review will verify measurement points reference outside conductor location per ECM standards once dimensions provided

details.text: No dimensioned clearance callouts appear on landscape plan between trees and overhead electric line. UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires clearances measured from outside (outer) conductor, not pole centerline. Without dimension callouts and notes specifying reference point, measurement methodology cannot be verified.

runComments.comment: UCM § 1.10.10.4 specifies clearances are measured from the outside (outer) electric conductor, not from pole centerline. The landscape plan (Sheet 31) contains no dimensioned clearance callouts between trees and the overhead electric line. Without explicit dimensions and notation indicating the measurement reference point, the measurement methodology cannot be verified.

Tree clearance measurements are not dimensioned on the landscape plan, preventing evaluation of measurement reference points. The grouping's measurement methodology requires that clearances be measured from the outside conductor (not pole centerline), which can be 4+ feet offset from the pole center due to cross arms. Without clearance dimensions shown on the plan, it cannot be verified whether any measurements that may have been made used the correct reference point (outside conductor vs. pole center). This item can only be evaluated if clearance dimensions are provided on submitted plans. Applicant must provide: (1) clearance dimensions from tree trunks to outside conductor locations (not pole centerline) for any trees shown within 25 feet of electric conductors.

Landscape plan does not include dimension lines or measurements showing clearances from specific trees to the OHE line. The tree locations and OHE line are shown graphically, but clearance distances are not dimensioned. Without explicit clearance dimensions, measurement reference points (pole centerline vs. outer conductor) cannot be verified.

details.text: Landscape plan does not include dimension lines terminating at tree trunk centers showing clearances to electric facilities. Measurements must reference trunk center (planting location), not canopy edge, per UCM § 1.10.10.4. Without dimensioned callouts, tree reference point cannot be verified.

runComments.comment: UCM § 1.10.10.4 specifies clearances are measured from tree trunk center (planting location), not tree canopy edge. The landscape plan (Sheet 31) shows tree symbols but contains no dimensioned clearance callouts or notes clarifying whether measurements terminate at trunk or canopy edge. Measurement reference point cannot be verified.

Tree clearance measurements are not dimensioned on the landscape plan, preventing evaluation of tree reference points. The grouping's measurement methodology requires that clearances be measured from tree trunk center (planting location), not from canopy edge. Without clearance dimensions shown on the plan, it cannot be verified whether measurements (if provided elsewhere) reference the correct tree location point. This item can only be evaluated if clearance dimensions appear on submitted plans. Applicant must provide: (1) clearance dimensions terminating at tree trunk center (planting location symbol) for any trees shown within clearance zones of electric facilities.

Landscape plan does not include dimensioned clearances showing measurements from trees to overhead electric facilities. Without dimension lines and callouts specifying clearance measurements, the reference point (trunk vs. canopy edge) cannot be evaluated.

details.text: Three mitigation trees positioned in southeast corner of landscape plan at approximately 2–5 feet from OHE line on southern property boundary cannot be verified for clearance compliance. Without dimensioned measurements and cross-reference to electrical plan showing conductor positions and clearance zones, distances cannot be verified.

runComments.comment: The landscape plan (Sheet 31) shows only the overhead electric (OHE) distribution line along the western property boundary. Critical electrical infrastructure is absent: underground electrical lines, transformer pads, utility poles, and pull boxes shown on the electrical design plan (Sheet 21) are not depicted on the landscape plan. The landscape plan is inadequate to allow verification of tree clearances from electric facilities.

Trees are shown on the landscape plan in relation to the overhead electric facilities (OHE line is depicted on Sheet 31 along the southern boundary), but the relationship cannot be meaningfully verified due to the deficiencies in EL-2.10 and EL-2.11. Specifically: (1) trees are not identified by species on the landscape plan, preventing verification of utility compatibility; (2) trees are not differentiated by mature height, preventing identification of large-tree clearance requirements; (3) no conductor positions are marked (showing only the OHE line, not the outside conductor location offset from the pole); (4) clearance distances are not dimensioned. While trees and the OHE line are both visible on Sheet 31, sufficient cross-reference information to verify compliance with electric facility clearance requirements is not provided. Applicant must cross-reference the landscape plan to the plant schedule and provide: (1) species identification for each tree; (2) mature height notation; (3) outside conductor location and offset dimensions; (4) measured clearance distances.

Three mitigation trees positioned at 2-5 feet from OHE line on southern property boundary cannot be verified for clearance compliance without cross-reference to electrical plan showing conductor locations and clearance zones. Landscape plan shows OHE line routing but does not overlay electrical infrastructure details, transmission easement boundaries, or utility pole locations with sufficient clarity to independently verify tree clearances from the landscape plan alone.

comments.headline: Electrical Infrastructure Not Overlaid on Landscape Plan
comments.summary: Electrical plan (Sheet 21) shows utility poles, transformer pads, underground lines, and pull boxes. Landscape plan (Sheet 31) does not depict or reference this infrastructure. Without overlays, tree clearance and root barrier requirements cannot be verified.
comments.crossDep: Electrical design team and Austin Energy to confirm equipment locations and access requirements for landscape plan overlay

details.text: Utility poles are not marked or identified on landscape plan (Sheet 31). While OHE line is shown, specific pole locations are not distinctly labeled. Measured clearances from trees to poles (10-foot minimum per UCM § 1.10.10.4) cannot be verified without pole locations.

runComments.comment: Utility poles are not clearly marked or identified on the landscape plan (Sheet 31). While the overhead electric (OHE) line is shown along the western boundary, specific pole locations are not distinctly labeled. Without clear pole identification, clearances from proposed trees cannot be verified.

Compliance with the 10-foot utility pole clearance requirement cannot be verified because utility poles are not shown on the landscape plan (Sheet 31). Vision analysis confirmed that the OHE line is depicted but no pole locations or symbols are visible on the landscape plan. The electrical design plan (Sheet 21) notes an existing OHE line on the western edge outside the property boundary, but does not show pole locations within or adjacent to the development site. Applicant must provide: (1) identification of all existing and proposed overhead electric utility pole locations shown on site plan or utility plan; (2) landscape plan showing pole locations if any exist within or adjacent to development site; (3) measured clearances from trees to pole centers if poles are present.

Landscape plan and electrical plan (Sheet 21) do not show utility pole locations explicitly marked or dimensioned. While overhead electric lines are depicted on the landscape plan, specific pole locations are not identified on either sheet, preventing verification of 10-foot clearance requirement from poles.

details.text: Five transformer pads with vault easements identified on electrical design plan (Sheet 21) are absent from landscape plan (Sheet 31). Trees may be proposed within 10 lateral feet of pad-mounted equipment. Clearances from pad perimeters and access doors to trees cannot be dimensioned without transformer pad locations shown on landscape plan.

runComments.comment: The electrical design plan (Sheet 21) identifies five transformer pads with vault easements. None of these transformer pad locations are shown on the landscape plan (Sheet 31). UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires trees to remain ≥10 lateral feet from pad-mounted equipment; without transformer pad locations visible on the landscape plan, clearances cannot be verified or demonstrated.

Trees may be proposed within 10 lateral feet of the transformer pad (pad-mounted electric equipment) shown on Sheet 9 near the western site boundary between Building 2 and Valley View Road. Vision analysis of the landscape plan (Sheet 31) indicates trees in close proximity to a 'rectangular pad structure' in this area. However, compliance cannot be verified because: (1) clearance distances from the transformer pad to tree trunks are not dimensioned on the landscape plan; (2) the exact location and footprint of the transformer pad is not referenced or dimensioned on the landscape plan; (3) no notation indicates access door orientation for pad-mounted equipment. Applicant must provide: (1) transformer pad location and footprint clearly marked on landscape plan with dimensions; (2) measured clearance distances from pad perimeter (and access door area if applicable) to each tree within 25 feet; (3) verification of 10-foot minimum clearance.

Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows transformer pads and electrical infrastructure with underground distribution, but the landscape plan (Sheet 31) does not clearly identify pad-mounted equipment locations or access door orientations in relation to proposed trees. Without explicit pad-mount locations on the landscape plan, the 10-foot clearance requirement cannot be verified.

details.text: Extensive underground electrical conduits, pull boxes, and vault easements shown on electrical plan (Sheet 21) are not depicted on landscape plan (Sheet 31). Trees are distributed throughout site above underground infrastructure. Clearances of ≥5 feet from underground equipment per UCM § 1.10.10.4 cannot be verified without underground utility locations overlaid on landscape plan.

runComments.comment: The electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows extensive underground electrical conduits, pull boxes, and vault easements. The landscape plan (Sheet 31) does not depict underground electrical lines, pull boxes, or vaults. UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires trees remain ≥5 lateral feet from underground electric equipment. Without underground utility locations shown on the landscape plan, clearances cannot be verified.

Trees are proposed throughout the site where underground electrical infrastructure (transformers, pull boxes, service lines) exists. Per Sheet 21, multiple underground transformer pads and pull boxes are located throughout the development serving each building. Sheet 31 shows trees distributed around the perimeter and near buildings, but clearance distances from underground equipment to tree locations are not dimensioned. The 5-foot minimum clearance requirement cannot be verified because: (1) underground equipment locations are not cross-referenced or overlay on the landscape plan; (2) no clearance dimensions are provided; (3) tree symbol locations cannot be precisely related to underground utility coordinates. Applicant must provide: (1) overlay of underground electric equipment locations (transformer pads, pull boxes) on landscape plan with coordinates; (2) measured clearance distances from each tree to nearest underground equipment; (3) verification that all trees maintain minimum 5-foot lateral clearance from underground equipment.

Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan) shows underground electric lines and pull boxes, but the landscape plan (Sheet 31) does not overlay underground equipment locations with sufficient clarity to verify 5-foot clearance from tree planting locations. Coordination between electrical and landscape plans is insufficient for verification.

details.text: Trees proposed within 20 lateral feet of underground electric equipment require 4-foot deep root barriers positioned 5 feet from equipment per UCM § 1.10.10.4. Without underground equipment locations shown on landscape plan, trees within the 20-foot clearance zone cannot be identified. Landscape details (Sheet 37) do not specify root barrier installation requirements or locations.

runComments.comment: UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires trees within 20 lateral feet of underground electric equipment to have root barriers (minimum 4 feet deep, positioned 5 feet from equipment). Underground electrical equipment is not shown on the landscape plan (Sheet 31), so which trees (if any) fall within the 20-foot zone cannot be determined. Additionally, no root barrier details are provided on the landscape plan.

Root barriers (minimum 4 feet deep, positioned 5 feet from equipment) are required for trees proposed within 20 lateral feet of underground electric equipment. Compliance cannot be verified for multiple reasons: (1) underground equipment locations are not clearly mapped on the landscape plan (see EL-2.8); (2) no clearance dimensions identify which trees are within the 20-foot zone; (3) landscape plan details and notes do not specify root barrier requirements or details; (4) tree locations cannot be precisely measured against underground equipment coordinates. Applicant must provide: (1) landscape plan identifying which trees are within 20 feet of underground equipment; (2) specification notes requiring 4-foot deep root barriers positioned 5 feet from equipment for affected trees; (3) landscape details showing root barrier installation specifications; (4) measured clearances documenting placement.

Landscape details (Sheet 37) and landscape plan (Sheet 31) do not show explicit root barrier specifications at trees planted near underground electric facilities. The landscape plan does not clearly identify which trees are within 20-foot clearance zone of underground equipment, and landscape details do not specify root barrier requirements (minimum 4 feet deep, positioned 5 feet from equipment).

comments.headline: Transmission Line Voltage & Easement Boundaries Not Specified
comments.summary: Overhead electric line voltage (distribution <60kV vs. transmission ≥60kV) is not documented, preventing verification of which clearance standards apply. Transmission easement boundaries are also not clearly marked on landscape plan. Electrical notes reference transmission structures on site.
comments.crossDep: Electrical engineer and Austin Energy to confirm voltage classification and transmission easement boundaries for site
comments.attn: Confirm whether transmission structures and easements are truly present on site vs. general reference in notes. These findings flagged by runs 2–3 only (no run 1).

details.text: Overhead electric line voltage classification (transmission ≥60kV vs. distribution <60kV) is not specified on any submitted plan. Transmission clearance requirements differ significantly from distribution requirements. Without voltage documentation, transmission rule applicability cannot be determined.

runComments.comment: Compliance with transmission conductor clearance requirements cannot be verified because the voltage classification of the overhead electric line is not specified on any submitted plan. Per the grouping regulatory overview, transmission facilities are energized at 60kV or higher; most overhead facilities on typical development sites are distribution (less than 60kV). Without voltage documentation, it cannot be determined whether the 50-foot transmission clearance requirement applies. Additionally, tree species cannot be identified from landscape plan symbols (see EL-2.1). Applicant must provide: (1) voltage classification of the OHE line; (2) species identification keyed to landscape plan symbols; (3) measured clearance distances if transmission.

Transmission structures confirmed to be present on or adjacent to site per Electric Transmission Notes (Sheet 3, Block 13). However, whether the OHE line shown on landscape plan is transmission or distribution voltage cannot be determined from plans provided. Without voltage classification, and without species verification for trees near OHE line, compliance with 50-foot transmission clearance for non-utility-compatible trees cannot be assessed.

details.text: Large trees (mature height 40+ feet) may be proposed within 50 lateral feet of overhead electric transmission conductor. Compliance cannot be verified because: (1) OHE voltage not specified (transmission applicability unknown); (2) landscape plan does not differentiate tree sizes or show mature heights; (3) clearance distances not measured. Electrical transmission notes (Sheet 3) reference transmission structures on or adjacent to site.

runComments.comment: Large trees (mature height 40+ feet) may be proposed within 50 lateral feet of overhead electric transmission conductor. Compliance cannot be verified due to three factors: (1) OHE voltage not specified, so transmission applicability unknown; (2) landscape plan does not differentiate tree sizes or show mature heights; (3) clearance distances from conductor not measured. Applicant must provide: (1) OHE voltage classification; (2) mature height notation for trees on landscape plan keyed to ECM Appendix F; (3) measured clearances if transmission voltage confirmed.

Transmission structures confirmed to be addressed in general notes (Sheet 3, Block 13). However, whether the OHE line on landscape plan represents transmission or distribution voltage is not specified. Without voltage classification and without species identification of specific trees, compliance with 50-foot transmission clearance for large trees cannot be assessed.

details.text: Transmission easement boundaries are not clearly marked with dimensions or notes on landscape plan (Sheet 31). Grading plan (Sheet 11) indicates electric easements are depicted but type (transmission vs. distribution) and boundaries are not clearly delineated. OHE line shown as dashed line but not explicitly identified as within or outside transmission easement.

runComments.comment: Trees may be proposed within transmission easement boundaries. Compliance cannot be verified because transmission easement boundaries are not clearly shown or labeled on the landscape plan (Sheet 31). The grading plan (Sheet 11) indicates that easements (including electric easements) are depicted, but the specific type (transmission vs. distribution), location, and boundaries are not clearly marked with dimensions or notes tied to the landscape plan. The existing OHE line is shown as a dashed line on Sheet 31 but is not explicitly identified as being within or outside a transmission easement boundary. Applicant must provide: (1) transmission easement boundaries clearly identified and dimensioned on landscape plan; (2) verification that no trees are shown within any transmission easement.

Grading plan indicates a transmission easement is addressed in the design (evidenced by Electric Transmission Notes on Sheet 3). However, the exact boundaries of the transmission easement are not clearly delineated on the landscape plan in relation to proposed tree locations. Without explicit transmission easement boundary marking on the landscape plan, the specific locations of any trees within the easement cannot be confirmed.

comments.headline: Austin Energy Approval Missing for Trees in Restricted Clearance Zones
comments.summary: Three mitigation trees in southeast corner are positioned 2–5 feet from the OHE line, placing them within prohibited clearance zones (15 feet for non-utility-compatible distribution trees; 25 feet for large distribution trees; 50 feet for transmission). No written Austin Energy approval documentation is evident.
comments.crossDep: Austin Energy must review and approve any trees proposed within restricted clearance zones per UCM § 1.10.10.3
comments.attn: Status dependent on resolution of species identification and clearance documentation (EL-2.1, EL-2.3, EL-2.12, EL-2.13). Once those are confirmed to place trees in restricted zones, this becomes a definitive fail requiring Austin Energy approval before site plan approval.

details.text: Three mitigation trees positioned in southeast corner at approximately 2–5 feet from overhead electric line on southern property boundary fall within prohibited clearance zones (15 feet for non-utility-compatible distribution trees, 25 feet for large distribution trees, 50 feet for transmission trees). No written Austin Energy approval documentation is provided in submitted plans or supplementary documents.

runComments.comment: The landscape plan shows proposed trees located near the overhead electric (OHE) distribution line along the western property boundary. No documentation of written approval from Austin Energy authorizing any trees within restricted clearance zones is evident in the site plan sheets or supplementary documents reviewed. Per the Master Comment Report, Electric Review references indicate Austin Energy review occurred (UCM § 1.10.10.3 & 4 cited), but no approval letters or exception authorizations are visible in the submitted materials.

Trees appear to be proposed within prohibited clearance zones based on visual proximity to the OHE line shown on the landscape plan, but Austin Energy written approval documentation is not provided or visible on any submitted plan sheets or supplementary documents reviewed. However, definitive determination of violation cannot be made without: (1) verified species identification and utility compatibility status; (2) actual measured clearance distances; (3) OHE voltage classification (distribution vs. transmission); (4) confirmation that trees are indeed in prohibited zones per calculated thresholds. While the vision analysis indicates trees along the southern boundary have canopies that 'directly overlap or touch' the OHE line, suggesting potential violation, the absence of required documentation (species, clearances, approval) combined with unverified measurements prevents a conclusive fail determination. STATUS: Not-verifiable pending resolution of EL-2.1, EL-2.2, EL-2.3, EL-2.4 deficiencies. If any of those items prove to show trees within prohibited zones, and no Austin Energy approval is produced, this item becomes a fail.

Three trees marked as mitigation trees in the southeast corner of the landscape plan are positioned at approximately 2-5 feet from the OHE line along the southern property boundary, placing them within restricted clearance zones (15 feet for distribution non-utility-compatible trees, 25 feet for distribution large trees, 50 feet for transmission). No documentation of Austin Energy written approval for planting trees in these locations is provided in the submitted plans, application documents, or supplementary documents reviewed.
